card.name: Domkach
card.tagline: Nagpuri wedding dance of joy and satire
card.profile: Domkach (or Damkach) is a folk dance of Bihar, Jharkhand and Nepal's Madhesh province, performed during wedding ceremonies; in Bihar it features in the Mithila and Bhojpur regions and in Jharkhand it is a Nagpuri folk dance (Wikipedia). The women and men of the bride's and groom's families form a semicircle holding each other's waists and dance to satirical, joyful songs accompanied by dholak and ghungroo (Wikipedia). In its classic Chotanagpur form, the women of the groom's family perform it through the night after the baraat (wedding procession) has departed, keeping themselves awake and entertained (EZCC).
card.insight: The dance is named after the Dambru/Dom musical instrument; Nagpuri Domkach is sub-classified into Ekharia, Dohri and Jhumta variants, and the wedding-season run extends from Deouthan in Kartik (Oct-Nov) to the Rath Yatra in Ashadh (Jun-Jul) (Wikipedia).
